summary: Kathleen Higgins is a philosopher who taught Conor Roddy. She served as a resident scholar at the Bellagio Center (1993), a visiting fellow at Australian National University and Canberra School of Music (1997), and Professor of Philosophy at UT Austin.

Kathleen Kenyon (1906–1978) was a historian and archaeologist. She studied at St Paul's Girls' School and Somerville College. She held positions at the University of London (~1935–1962), the UCL Institute of Archaeology (1948–1962), and St Hugh's College (1962–1973).

Kathleen M. Erndl (1954–2017) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who taught Cameron Bailey and Lindsay G. McCune. She held posts at University of Wisconsin-Madison, DePauw University, Lewis & Clark College (~1987–1993), and Florida State University (~1993–2017).

Kathleen McDonald (b. 1952) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Ribur Rinpoche.
Kathrin Holz works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Würzburg under Ingo Strauch and holds a research affiliation at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Kathryn H. Selig Brown is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She earned her PhD from the University of Michigan by 2000, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Walter M. Spink.
Kathryn R. Blackstone is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She held posts at Victoria University of Wellington (attested 1998) and the University of Manitoba (attested 1999).

Katia Buffetrille (b. 1948) is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. She completed her PhD at Paris Nanterre University under Alexander W. Macdonald. She held posts at the EPHE, CRCAO, and as editor for Études mongoles, sibériennes, centrasiatiques et tibétaines.

Katragadda Paddayya (b. 1943) is an archaeologist and Indologist. After completing his doctoral degree at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1964–1968), he spent his career at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1973–2008), including as Professor of Geo-archaeology.

Katsuhiko Kamimura (1944–2003) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara and the University of Madras under V. Raghavan. He taught at Kokugakuin University and the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.
Katsuhiro Yoshizawa (b. 1945) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Doshisha University (~1965–1969) and served as a professor at Hanazono University (~1996–2016).

Katsuji Fujioka (1872–1935) was a linguist who taught Naoshiro Tsuji. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1894–1897) and the University of Leipzig (1901–1905), and later served as an assistant professor at the University of Tokyo (1910–1933).
Katsumi Kuroita (1874–1946) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1893 to 1896 and held a post there from ~1901 to 1935.

Katsumi Mimaki (b. 1947) is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University, INALCO, and the University of Paris. He served as a professor at Kyoto University (1996–2010) and became a member of the Japan Academy.

Katsumi Okimoto (1943–2014) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Tibetology. A graduate student at the University of Tokyo (~1970–1973), he served as a professor (~1985–2008), director, and professor emeritus (~2008–2014) at Hanazono University.

Katsumi Tanabe (b. 1941) is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1960–1967) and held academic posts at Kanazawa University (~1994–2002) and Chuo University (~2002–2012).

Katsutoshi Ono (1905–1988) was an archaeologist, Sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied and worked at Kyoto University. He also held posts at the Academy of Oriental Culture, Nara National Museum, Ryukoku University (~1965–1980), and Kansai University.

Kavita Singh (1964–2023) was an art historian and Indologist. She studied at Lady Shri Ram College, MSU Baroda, and Panjab University. She held posts at Marg Publications, San Diego Museum of Art, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, where she served as dean.

Kazi Dawa Samdup (1868–1922) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Bhutia Boarding School under Ugyen Gyatso and Tshampa Norbu, later serving as its headmaster (~1906–1919) and as a lecturer at the University of Calcutta (1920).

Kazu Uehara (1924–2017) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed studies at Kyushu University, worked as a full-time lecturer at the University of Miyazaki, and was a professor emeritus at Seijo University (~1967–1995).
